title: Streamline table density presets and resize gestures for large datasets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Redwood's table component currently has fractured behaviour across density modes and column-resize interactions. Users report jumpy column layouts when virtualization is enabled, unclear resize affordances on touch/trackpad, and inconsistencies between token-driven spacing across Compact/Default/Comfortable modes. This causes layout regressions in the Console where datasets exceed 5k rows and engineers request workarounds in product routes.

Goals:
- Define cohesive density presets (Compact / Default / Comfortable) backed by tokens that map consistently to row height, cell padding, and hit targets.
- Surface a deterministic resize gesture that works with virtualization (no jitter when unmounting/recycling rows) and across input types (mouse, touch, keyboard).
- Ensure sorting/filtering affordances remain discoverable at small densities (icons, hover targets, focus states).
- Provide accessible semantics for resize handles and density switches.
- Deliver final tokens + specs for engineering handoff and a lightweight Figma kit update.

Scope / Acceptance Criteria:
1) Density tokens: spacing-token names and values published (row-height, cell-vertical-padding, control-gap) and integrated into the component story.
2) Resize behaviour: dragging a column edge should update a top-level column model (not per-virtual-row), preview indicator visible, and commit persisted via onColumnResize event. No visual jitter during virtualization re-render.
3) Touch / trackpad: implement an expanded touch-hotzone (min 16px) and a long-press-to-resize fallback recommended for touch-only devices.
4) Sorting/filtering: small-density layout keeps icons visible; provide compact icon variants and increased hover target.
5) Accessibility: resize handle is keyboard operable (arrow keys adjust width in 4px steps), screen reader text provided, role=separator and aria-orientation supported.
6) Deliver Figma components + token doc + example Console screen updated.

Design proposals considered (shortlist):
- Option A (Token-first): Create three explicit tokens per density and wire them into the table component. Pros: predictable mapping; cons: needs broader token review.
- Option B (Adaptive height): Let the table compute height based on font-size + padding multipliers. Pros: flexible; cons: may produce rounding differences across browsers.
- Option C (CSS container queries): Use container queries to switch density visuals. Pros: responsive; cons: not fully supported in some environments.

Decision (so far): Proceed with Option A token-first approach, with a thin compatibility layer that allows an adaptive multiplier for experimental routes. We'll avoid heavy reliance on container queries to reduce cross-environment variability.

Implementation notes for engineering:
- Column model must be authoritative for width; virtualization should read widths from a single shared store (not from DOM node widths per row).
- Provide a visual preview (overlay guidelines) while resizing; commit after mouseup/touchend to avoid layout thrash.
- Use token names: token.table.rowHeight.compact, token.table.rowHeight.default, token.table.rowHeight.comfortable; token.table.cellPadding.*; token.table.resizeHotZone.
- Keyboard control: left/right arrow to decrement/increment by 4px while focus is on the separator; Home/End set min/max width.

Deliverables:
- Updated token table (tokens doc link)
- Figma kit: density presets + resize handle states (idle, hover, active, keyboard)
- Annotated spec for engineering including edge cases (pinned columns, column-reorder + resize interactions)
- QA checklist and accessibility notes

Rollout plan:
1) Ship token + spec to engineering (ETA 2026-03-12).
2) Engineering implements shared column model and exposes events (2026-03-13 to 2026-03-20).
3) Design review and visual QA with Console team (2026-03-21 to 2026-03-24).

Metrics to monitor post-release:
- Reduction in layout-related Console bugs (target: -50% in 30 days).
- Number of support tickets mentioning table cropping/jitter.
- Adoption: percent of Console routes updated to use new tokens.

Notes / Risks:
- If engineering prefers per-cell width measurement (for compatibility with existing implementations), expect additional dev time to reconcile virtualization jitter.
- Touch long-press proposal needs research for interfering with selection gestures on rows.

- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/redwood-tables-density-kit (prototype frames: density presets, resize-states)
- Design spec (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/987654321/Table+Density+and+Resize+Spec

comments: 2026-03-02 — Aisha: Initial discovery complete. Ran inventory across Console routes; 17 unique table usages identified. Captured visual regressions where virtualization + manual width were combined.
2026-03-04 — Miguel: Spiked a prototype that centralizes column widths in a shared React context. Preliminary patch reduces jitter but needs keyboard handling and touch hotzone work.
2026-03-06 — UX Review (Leah Kim): Prefer token-first to keep other components consistent. Requested explicit accessibility section in the spec. Added keyboard adjustment steps.

2026-03-08 — Eng feedback (Ravi Shah): Backend side already persists column preferences; we'll wire onColumnResize to existing user-preferences endpoint. Raised potential race condition with autosave debounce.
2026-03-10 — Aisha: Decided on token names and provided Figma frames for Compact/Default/Comfortable. Uploaded annotated specs to Confluence. Ready for handoff to eng on 2026-03-12.
